newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BOSNICH ESCAPES PROSECUTION OVER NAZI SALUTE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOSNICH ESCAPES PROSECUTION OVER NAZI SALUTE.

text.p: Aston Villa goalkeeper Mark Bosnich said on Friday he felt vindicated by a British Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) decision not to charge him in connection with the Nazi salute he made in front of Tottenham fans in October.
"I am just thankful for the people who have shown some common sense...I feel vindicated," the Australian goalkeeper said.
"So far as I am concerned, anyone with half a brain knew what it was all about and the Football Association (F.A.) and now the CPS have taken a common sense point of view."
Bosnich was fined 1,000 pounds ($1,650) by the F.A . for misconduct after giving the raised-arm salute in front of Spurs fans, many of whom are from North London's large Jewish community.
He publicly apologised for his gesture, made after fans baited him over an incident 18 months previously when he had knocked Tottenham striker Juergen Klinsmann unconscious in a rash challenge.
Bosnich said he was unaware of Tottenham's traditional Jewish support and had made the gesture as a joke in reference to Klinsmann's nationality.
The CPS decision comes as a timely boost for Bosnich, who is close to a first-team comeback with Villa after being sidelined since October following knee surgery.
